newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil firm, looks to China.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil firm, looks to China.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps extended their early day gains late afternoon on Thursday on expectations that prices might have bottomed and fresh demand might emerge from China after the handover of Hong Kong, traders said.
"Gas oil is stronger because people are expecting China to come back into the market for July or August cargoes," one trader said.
July swaps were quoted at $22.55/$22.65 per barrel, August at $23.00/$23.10, both up about 20 and 25 cents, respectively, from Wednesday, brokers said.
July swaps traded earlier in the day at $22.50 per barrel with more trades heard for August with deals at $22.97, $22.99 and $23.00, brokers said.
Firmer August prices have widened the July/August contango to value at about 50 cents from 40 cents on Wednesday, they said.
The stronger August prices were attributed to market expectations that demand will pick up by then as Chinese buying returns to normal.
China halved its April imports over March to about 400,000 tonnes. May imports are expected around that level.
Traders were counting on higher Chinese imports in the third quarter as most felt that the low second quarter imports has lead to lower stocks among Chinese endusers.
Sources also said they expected smuggling actitives to pick up post-handover as the Chinese authorities ease up their current tough crackdown.
Others are also looking towards firmer levels as a correction to the recent large falls as new supply sources such as arbitrage cargoes from the West are closed.

The swaps regrade remained wide on buying from a trader looking to hedge his sale to Taiwan for 32,000 tonnes of jet fuel for Aug 1-10 delivery at just under $197.00 per tonne on a cost-and-freight basis, traders said.
July swaps regrade was bid unchanged at $2.00 per barrel while August was quoted up about five cents at $1.80/$2.10 from Wednesday.
Fuel oil edged up slightly in active trade with July last quoted $100.00/$100.75 per tonne. July traded earlier in the day at $100.25 and $100.50, brokers said.
